title: Context fragmentation reading sprint — notes & loose hypotheses
content:
Quick background and why I care:
- Problem: long interactions get internally "fragmented" across KV caches / windowing heuristics leading to brittle retrieval and weird topical drift.
- Motivation: product examples (customer X chat history + doc search) — we see hallucination spikes when important short-lived context is evicted. This seems strongly correlated with infrequent but high-salience tokens (e.g., single-line system instructions, billing/mfa codes).

What I read (high level):
- Paper A (notes): incremental attention / rolling attention windows — claims gradual forgetting can be ameliorated by content-aware retention. Implementation complexity: needs saliency scoring at token time.
- Blog post B: pragmatic heuristics for session stitching in web chat — uses recency-weighted importance + entity tagging to keep critical lines.
- Workshop slides C: KV-sharding and eviction strategies for multi-tenant runtimes — highlights the latency vs memory tradeoffs for aggressive per-request eviction.

Most interesting fragments / quotations: (copy-paste from sources)
- "Preserve tokens with high cross-attention footprint, not just recency." (paper A)
- "A small set of tokens carries most instruction signal; losing them collapses behavior." (slides C)

Loose hypotheses we can test (ranked):
1) Local importance scoring: scoring each token by peak attention weight across next N steps and pinning top-k tokens per session will reduce hallucinations on task-oriented dialogues by >10% measured on our eval set. (easy-ish: we can instrument sampling of attention weights during offline runs and retroactively compute scores)
2) Entity anchors: named entities and 1-gram tokens that start with uppercase/digits (codes) are disproportionately important; simple regex+ner hybrid will yield quick wins. (cheap)
3) Gradient-saliency proxy: approximate importance via gradient w.r.t logits at generation time — may be too expensive for production but worth doing offline to validate.

Initial experiments I want to run (practical steps):
- Offline pass on 10k chat sessions (v2 eval corpus): replay generation using tracer that logs cross-attention max per token (for first 256 tokens after event). Compute token importance distribution, produce retention policy: top-3 tokens per 1k window. Compare generations with baseline. (metric: answer F1, hallucination rate, avg latency)
- Heuristic pilot: entity-anchor retention in our Redwood hosted demo (small internal model) toggled via request flag. Run A/B for 1k sessions. Measure regression.
- Simulation of eviction sequences: simulate aggressive LRU vs importance-pin vs hybrid and measure when instruction tokens drop out.

Operational constraints and product tradeoffs:
- Cost: pinning tokens increases KV memory footprint per session; for a high-scale product this interacts with Dedicated sizing. Need modeling of per-session footprint increase vs overall p99 latency.
- Security: pinned tokens could include PII — tie into KMS/audit expectations; need opt-in or auto-scrub for private deploys.
- Rollouts: feature gate at route level (hosted) + config knobs on Dedicated auto-scaling suggestions (in Redwood Console).

Edge cases that worry me:
- Adversarial sessions that artificially inflate token importance by spamming attention (someone could craft tokens to be pinned). Need budget per-session or per-user pin cap.
- Interaction with quantized kernels: pinned KV entries stored in compressed format — will quantization noise change attention footprint? need to test across q4/q8 modes.

Notes-to-self for implementation design doc:
- API surface: new optional field in generation request 'pin_policy' with values: off|heuristic|attention-proxy. Provide 'pin_quota' and 'pin_ttl'.
- Runtime: sampling mode where attention logging is cheap — maybe keep max-attention per token using int16 counters rather than full float logs to reduce overhead.
- Console UI: show pinned tokens per-session in traces, with reason flags (NER, attention-score, manual).

Related artifacts and places to talk to folks:
- GH issue: kv-cache-experiments#142 (linked above) — Omar is already experimenting with LRU variants.
- Slack: #applied-ml — started thread on 2026-09-30 with preliminary results from demo.
- People: ping Mika for quantization interaction tests; Evelyn for eval design (we need a well-defined hallucination label set).

Open questions (unresolved):
- What is the right budget for pinned tokens before we start harming latency/cost? (simulate + model)
- Can we produce a cheap importance proxy with token-level features (pos, ner, length, recency, generation-confidence) that approximates attention-derived scores with >0.8 correlation? If yes, productionizable.
- For private deployments, how much TTL variability do customers want? Some want indefinite pinning for compliance; others want ephemeral. Need policy model.

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- Week 1: run offline replay tracer job on 10k sessions (I'll own). Deliver: token importance distribution + top-3 retention policy simulation results. (due 2026-10-19)
- Week 2: spin up entity-anchor heuristic A/B on internal demo. Coordinate with Omar for routing flag and Mika for quantization smoke test. (due 2026-10-26)
- Draft a one-pager for product: short description, expected unit-cost delta, rollout safety knobs. (share with product-hosted-api for feedback)

Random observations and scribbles:
- Could combine with Redwood Optimize signals: use past workload to infer which tokens are commonly reused across sessions (global anchors) and compress them into a shared read-only cache to reduce per-session pin cost.
- If we expose pin policy, default should be "heuristic" with a conservative pin_quota=4 to avoid surprises.

References (short list):
- arXiv:2102.xxxxx (attention retention paper) — concept: cross-attention footprint.
- Blog: session-stitching-guide.blog/2025 (heuristics & examples)
- Internal: GH:kv-cache-experiments/issue/142; Confluence: context-fragmentation-hypotheses-iman

Notes end. Will iterate after initial replay results. Keep this doc as living scratchpad for experiment logs and raw tracer dumps (compressed) — do not copy into final design doc until we have clear numbers.
